text: Let A and B be 3 $\times$ 3 real matrices such that A is symmetric matrix and B is skew-symmetric matrix. Then the system of linear equations $(A^{2}B^{2}$ $-$ $B^{2}A^{2}) X = O$, where X is a 3 $\times$ 1 column matrix of unknown variables and O is a 3 $\times$ 1 null matrix, has :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A^{T}=A$ and $B^{T}=-B$, so $(A^{2})^{T}=(A^{T})^{2}=A^{2}$ and $(B^{2})^{T}=(B^{T})^{2}=(-B)^{2}=B^{2}$.

Let $P=A^{2}B^{2}-B^{2}A^{2}$. Then

$P^{T}=(B^{2})^{T}(A^{2})^{T}-(A^{2})^{T}(B^{2})^{T}=B^{2}A^{2}-A^{2}B^{2}=-P,$

so $P$ is a $3\times 3$ skew-symmetric matrix.

For a skew-symmetric matrix of odd order, $|P|=|P^{T}|=|-P|=(-1)^{3}|P|=-|P|$, so $|P|=0$.

$PX=O$ is a homogeneous system, so it always has the solution $X=O$; since $|P|=0$, it also has non-zero solutions, and hence infinitely many solutions.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: Let f be a twice differentiable function defined on R such that f(0) = 1, f'(0) = 2 and f'(x) $\neq$ 0 for all x $\in$ R. If $\left |\begin{array}{ll} f(x) & f^{'}(x) \\ f^{'}(x) & f^{''}(x) \end{array}\right |$ = 0, for all x$\in$R, then the value of f(1) lies in the interval :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left |\begin{array}{ll} f(x) & f^{'}(x) \\ f^{'}(x) & f^{''}(x) \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow f(x).f^{''}(x)-(f^{'}(x))^{2}=0$

Dividing by $(f(x))^{2}$, we get

$\Rightarrow \frac{f(x).f^{''}(x)-(f^{'}(x))^{2}}{(f(x))^{2}}=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{d}{dx}\left (\frac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}\right )=0$

Integrating both side, 

$\frac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}=c$ (constant)

At, $x=0$, $\frac{f^{'}(0)}{f(0)}=c$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{1}=c$

$\Rightarrow c=2$

$\therefore$ $\frac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}=2$

$\Rightarrow \int \frac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}dx=2\int dx$

$\Rightarrow \ln |f(x)|=2x+c^{'}$

at x = 0,

$\ln |f(0)|=0+c^{'}$

$\Rightarrow 0=0+c^{'}$

$\Rightarrow c^{'}=0$

$\therefore$ $\ln |f(x)|=2x$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=e^{2x}$

$f(1)=e^{2}=(2.71)^{2}=7.34$

So it lie between (6, 9).

text: If P is a point on the parabola $y = x^{2} + 4$ which is closest to the straight line y = 4x $-$ 1, then the co-ordinates of P are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, curve $y = x^{2} + 4$

and, line y = 4x $-$ 1

Here, $y = x^{2} + 4$


[IMG]

$\therefore$ $\frac{dy}{dx}=2x$ ..... (i)

and y = 4x $-$ 1

$\frac{dy}{dx}=4$ ..... (ii)

Let the required point be $P(x_{1}, y_{1})$.

$\therefore$ $\frac{dy}{dx}\left |_{P}=2x_{1} \right.$ ..... (iii)

$\because$ Slopes will be equal.

$\therefore$ $2x_{1} = 4$ [from Eqs. (ii) and (iii)]

$\Rightarrow x_{1}=\frac{4}{2}=2$

Now, the given point $P(x_{1}, y_{1})$ lies on curve $y = x^{2} + 4$,

$\therefore$ $y_{1} = x{}_{1}^{2}$ + 4

$\Rightarrow$ $y_{1} = 2^{2} + 4 = 8$

Hence, required coordinate of P = (2, 8)

text: The probability that two randomly selected subsets of the set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} have exactly two elements in their intersection, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, set P = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}

Let the two subsets be A and B

Then, n (A $\cap$ B) = 2 (as given in question)

We can choose two elements from set P in $^{5}C_{2}$ ways.

After choosing two common elements for set A and B, each of remaining three elements from set P have three choice (1) It can go to set A (2) It can go to set B (3) It don't go to any sets it stays at set P.

$\therefore$ Total ways for the three elements = 3 $\times$ 3 $\times$ $3 = 3^{3}$

$\therefore$ Required probability = $\frac{{}^{5}C_{2}\times 3^{3}}{(2^{5})(2^{5})}$ = $\frac{{}^{5}C_{2}\times 3^{3}}{4^{5}}=\frac{10\times 27}{2^{10}}=\frac{135}{2^{9}}$

text: Let a point P be such that its distance from the point (5, 0) is thrice the distance of P from the point ($-$5, 0). If the locus of the point P is a circle of radius r, then $4r^{2}$ is equal to $________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let P(h, k)

Given

PA = 3PB

$PA^{2} = 9PB^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ (h $-$ $5)^{2} + k^{2} = 9$[$(h + 5)^{2} + k^{2}$]

$\Rightarrow$ $8h^{2} + 8k^{2} + 100h + 200 = 0$

$\therefore$ Locus

$x^{2}+y^{2}+\left (\frac{25}{2}\right )x+25=0$

$\therefore$ $c\equiv \left (\frac{-25}{4},0\right )$

$\therefore$ $r^{2}=\left (\frac{-25}{4}\right )^{2}-25$

$=\frac{625}{16}-25$

$=\frac{225}{16}$

$\therefore$ $4r^{2}=4\times \frac{225}{16}=\frac{225}{4}=56.25$

After Round of $4r^{2} = 56$

Distance between skew lines $=\frac{\left [\vec{a}_{2}-\vec{a}_{1}\vec{b}_{1}\vec{b}_{2}\right ]}{\left |\vec{b}_{1}\times \vec{b}_{2}\right |}$

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} λ & \frac{1}{2}+2λ & -λ \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right |$

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right |–$

$=\frac{\left |-5λ-\frac{3}{2}\right |}{\sqrt{14}}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2\sqrt{2}}$

$=|10λ+3|=7\Rightarrow λ=-1$

$\Rightarrow |λ|=1$

text: The number of the real roots of the equation $(x+1)^{2}+|x-5|=\frac{27}{4}$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When $x>5$

$(x+1)^{2}+(x-5)=\frac{27}{4}$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+3x-4=\frac{27}{4}$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+3x-\frac{43}{4}=0$

$\Rightarrow 4x^{2}+12x-43=0$

$x=\frac{-12\pm \sqrt{144+688}}{8}$

$x=\frac{-12\pm \sqrt{832}}{8}=\frac{-12\pm 28.8}{8}$

$=\frac{-3+7.2}{2}$

$=\frac{-3+7.2}{2},\frac{-3-7.2}{2}$ 

= 2.1, -5.1 [ both are rejected as x should be > 5 ]

(Therefore no solution)

For $x\leq 5$

$(x+1)^{2}-(x-5)=\frac{27}{4}$

$x^{2}+x+6-\frac{27}{4}=0$

$4x^{2}+4x-3=0$

$x=\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{16+48}}{8}$

$x=\frac{-4\pm 8}{8}\Rightarrow x=-\frac{12}{8},\frac{4}{8}$

$\therefore$ So, the equation have two real roots.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: The students $S_{1}, S_{2}, ....., S_{10}$ are to be divided into 3 groups A, B and C such that each group has at least one student and the group C has at most 3 students. Then the total number of possibilities of forming such groups is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let group C have $r$ students, $r=1,2,3$; they are chosen in ${}^{10}C_{r}$ ways.

Each of the remaining $10-r$ students goes to A or B in $2^{10-r}$ ways; removing the 2 ways in which A or B is empty leaves $2^{10-r}-2$ ways.

$r=1$: ${}^{10}C_{1}\qquad (2^{9}-2)=10\times 510=5100$

$r=2$: ${}^{10}C_{2}\qquad (2^{8}-2)=45\times 254=11430$

$r=3$: ${}^{10}C_{3}\qquad (2^{7}-2)=120\times 126=15120$

$\text{Total}=5100+11430+15120=31650$

Hence, the answer is 31650.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift
